structures.title: The basic SOV statement
structures.explanation: Hindi's default order puts the verb last, after the subject and object. The conjugated verb agrees with the subject in gender and number, and its auxiliary (हूँ/है/हैं) closes the sentence. Get comfortable ending every clause with a verb.

structures.title: Saying from, by, or with
structures.explanation: The postposition से follows a noun to mean 'from' (source), 'by' (means), or 'with' (instrument/company). It comes after the noun and triggers the oblique case on that noun.

structures.title: Marking to / for / a specific object
structures.explanation: को follows a noun to mark the recipient ('to/for') or a definite/animate direct object. With time words it means 'at'. Pronouns fuse with it: मुझ+को = मुझे, उस+को = उसे.

structures.title: Locating in or on something
structures.explanation: में means 'in/inside' and पर means 'on/at a surface'. Both are postpositions placed after the (oblique) noun. Choose में for containment and पर for contact or a point.
structures.ex1_ref: The book is in the bag.
structures.ex2_ref: The cat is on the roof.

structures.title: Expressing wants and likes
structures.explanation: For wanting or liking, the experiencer takes को/मुझे and the thing is the grammatical subject, so the verb agrees with the thing, not the person. चाहिए = need/want; पसंद है = like.

structures.title: Forming a yes/no question
structures.explanation: Put क्या at the start of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question; word order otherwise stays the same. In speech a rising intonation alone can also do the job.

structures.title: The perfective-past ने pattern
structures.explanation: With transitive verbs in the perfective past, the subject takes ने and the verb agrees with the object in gender and number. Intransitive verbs (जाना, आना) never take ने.

structures.title: Negating a statement
structures.explanation: Place नहीं directly before the verb to negate a statement. The auxiliary है/हैं is often dropped after नहीं in the present. Use न for softer negation and मत for negative commands.

structures.title: Comparing two things
structures.explanation: To say A is more ___ than B, name A, then 'B से' (than B), then optionally ज़्यादा (more), then the adjective. The adjective itself does not change for comparison; से carries the 'than'.
structures.ex1_target: सेब संतरे से ज़्यादा महँगा है।
structures.ex1_ref: The apple is more expensive than the orange.

structures.title: Building a relative clause
structures.explanation: Hindi links clauses with the relative–correlative pair जो...वह ('the one who... that one'). The जो-clause usually comes first and names the thing; the वह-clause makes the main statement.
structures.ex1_target: जो आदमी यहाँ रहता है, वह डॉक्टर है।
structures.ex1_ref: The man who lives here is a doctor.
structures.ex2_target: जो तुमने कहा, वह सच है।

structures.title: Expressing obligation
structures.explanation: Use को/मुझे + the infinitive (-ना) + है for 'have to', or + पड़ता है for stronger external compulsion. The infinitive may agree with a following object in some styles.
structures.ex2_target: मुझे रोज़ काम करना पड़ता है।
structures.ex2_ref: I have to work every day.

structures.title: Giving a reason
structures.explanation: क्योंकि (because) introduces the cause after the result; इसलिए (therefore/so) introduces the result after the cause. Pick the connector based on which clause comes first.
structures.ex1_target: मैं घर पर हूँ क्योंकि मैं बीमार हूँ।
structures.ex1_ref: I am at home because I am sick.
structures.ex2_target: बारिश हो रही थी, इसलिए हम नहीं गए।
structures.ex2_ref: It was raining, so we didn't go.

structures.title: Talking about the future
structures.explanation: Add the future ending (-ऊँगा/एगा/एँगे) to the verb; the -गा/गी/गे part agrees in gender and number. Use it for plans and predictions.
structures.ex1_ref: I will go to Delhi tomorrow.
structures.ex2_ref: They will come in the evening.

structures.title: Describing an action in progress
structures.explanation: For the present continuous, put रहा/रही/रहे (agreeing with the subject) between the verb stem and the auxiliary है/हैं. It marks an action happening right now.
structures.ex1_target: मैं अभी खाना खा रहा हूँ।

structures.title: Expressing the superlative
structures.explanation: सबसे literally means 'than all', so सबसे + adjective = 'the most ___'. Place it before the adjective; no change to the adjective ending beyond normal gender agreement.
structures.ex1_target: वह कक्षा में सबसे लंबा है।
structures.ex1_ref: He is the tallest in the class.
structures.ex2_target: यह शहर का सबसे अच्छा होटल है।
structures.ex2_ref: This is the best hotel in the city.

structures.title: Making a conditional sentence
structures.explanation: अगर (if) opens the condition and तो (then) opens the result. For real/likely conditions use normal future/present verbs; अगर can be dropped in speech but तो usually stays.
structures.ex1_target: अगर समय होगा तो मैं आऊँगा।
structures.ex1_ref: If I have time, I will come.
